_comment: Windows where the filing rate says something about US, not about the code.
Read by tools/ticket_flow.py and shaded on the website's ticket-flow charts.
Add a window whenever a deliberate campaign, an import, or any other
bookkeeping event moves the curve. An unmarked one makes the chart read as
'the code got much worse, then much better' when nothing of the sort
happened -- which is worse than not publishing the chart at all.
kind: 'sweep'  a deliberate bulk-discovery campaign. Real bugs, found
because we went looking; the filing rate is a measure of
kind: 'import' bookkeeping. Tickets written down in bulk for work that
already existed; nothing was discovered that day.
tracks: which lanes the window applies to; omit or use '*' for all.

sweeps.label: board created
sweeps.note: The day devdocs/progress/ was founded: 398 of the board's tickets were written down at once, for work that had been in flight since 2026-05-24. Nothing was discovered on this date. Every 'filed' curve starts with this cliff and it means bookkeeping, not defects.

sweeps.label: CPython differential sweep
sweeps.note: Deliberate bulk discovery: Nil-Python run against CPython and every divergence filed. Peaked at 47 tickets on 2026-08-02. The bugs are real; the RATE is a measure of how hard we looked, so the fall afterwards is not the code improving.
